title: The Park Report
covers: how to choose an equation for one exact value or an inequality for a range of values, solve the model, and check that the answer makes sense
cert: choosing an equation or an inequality to model a real problem, solving it and checking it

intro.caption: Lesson 8-7 — choosing an equation or an inequality to solve real problems. Odalys writes the Screamline Park News. Today she must file the incident report. Three gates and a boss stand between her and the front page.

balloons.t: Today's incident report. Every incident gets a math model. No guessing. Rules are rules.
Equation or inequality? A good reporter asks first.
Most of these incidents are about me. I'm famous.
Bandit hit 3 stands. Same number from each. 24 funnel cakes, exactly!
"Exactly 24" is one total. But other clues say "no more than." Those can't use the same model.

pages.caption: Some clues give ONE exact value: use an equation (=). Others give a limit, a constraint with a range of values: use an inequality (<, >, ≤, ≥).

balloons.t: Splash Boat: no more than 12 riders. 5 are seated. Stop!
So how many more can get on? Is that = or ≤?
I split the refund money equally among 4 families. Each got $15. My poor heart.
That's m ÷ 4 = 15. Time to solve every model.
A report can't just have numbers. Every answer has to make sense in the story.
I solved one too! I got 325 balloons per bunch. Is that a lot?
Two more incidents. Then it prints.

pages.caption: Odalys has a plan: model first, then solve, then check.

win.caption: Read the clue first. One exact value? Write an equation. A limit like "at least" or "no more than"? Write an inequality. Then solve with inverse operations and check that the answer makes sense.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Choose the Model
gates.prompt: Each incident needs the right model. Look for the key words: exactly, is, in all mean one value. At least, no more than, fewer than mean a range.
hints: Conceptual: an equation says two sides are the same, so it has one answer. An inequality shows a constraint, so many values can work.
Procedural: find the key words in the clue. Then decide the operation: same amount from each group is multiplication, more added on is addition.

steps: Practice clue: "The prize booth gave out at least 40 bears."
"At least" is a limit, not one exact number. So this needs an inequality.
Let b be the bears given out: b ≥ 40.
worked.q: "A number plus 9 is 30." Equation or inequality?

items.q: Bandit took the same number of funnel cakes, c, from each of 3 stands. He took exactly 24 in all. Which model fits?

options.fb: "Exactly 24" is one total. ≤ would let him take fewer than 24, like 12.
The same number from each of 3 stands is 3 groups of c. That is multiplication, not adding 3.
> means MORE than 24. The clue says exactly 24, one value.

items.q: The Splash Boat holds no more than 12 riders. 5 are seated. Which model shows how many more riders, r, can board?

options.fb: = says exactly 7 more MUST board. "No more than" also allows fewer, so it is a range.
≥ means 12 or more riders. That breaks the limit. "No more than" is ≤.
5r means 5 groups of r. The 5 seated riders are added to the new riders, not multiplied.
"Fewer than" is a limit, so it needs the symbol <. That is an inequality.

options.t: "Every rider must be at least 48 inches"
options.fb: "At least" is a limit, so it needs ≥. That is an inequality.

options.t: "The line holds no more than 40 people"
options.fb: "No more than" is a limit, so it needs ≤. That is an inequality.

options.t: "Two mascot heads weigh exactly 9 pounds in all"

gates.pass: Odalys sorts the clues: "exactly" goes to equations, limits go to inequalities. Rafi: "So it IS ≤. Good. The boat stays afloat."

gates.title: Gate 2 · Solve the Models
gates.prompt: Solve each model from the report. Use the inverse operation on both sides.
hints: Conceptual: equations and inequalities are solved the same way. Undo the operation on both sides to get the variable alone.
Procedural: the inverse of × is ÷, the inverse of ÷ is ×, and the inverse of + is −. Do the same step to both sides.

steps: The inverse of subtracting 14 is adding 14: m = 26 + 14 = 40.

items.label: Funnel cakes · 3c = 24, so c =
items.aria: funnel cakes taken from each stand

fb.msg: 72 is 24 × 3. The inverse of multiplying by 3 is DIVIDING by 3.
21 is 24 − 3. 3c means 3 times c, so divide by 3.

items.label: Splash Boat · r + 5 ≤ 12, so r ≤
items.aria: the most riders who can still board

fb.msg: 17 is 12 + 5. Undo + 5 by subtracting 5 from both sides.

items.fbDefault: Subtract 5 from both sides of r + 5 ≤ 12.

items.label: Refunds · m ÷ 4 = 15, so m = $

fb.msg: 3.75 is 15 ÷ 4. The inverse of dividing by 4 is MULTIPLYING by 4.
19 is 15 + 4. m ÷ 4 means m split into 4 parts, so multiply by 4.

items.fbDefault: Multiply both sides of m ÷ 4 = 15 by 4.

gates.pass: 8 cakes per stand, up to 7 more riders, and $60 in refunds. Mr. Krank whispers, "Sixty dollars..."

gates.title: Gate 3 · Does It Make Sense?
gates.prompt: A good report explains what each answer means and checks that it is reasonable.
hints: Conceptual: an equation answer is one value. An inequality answer is a range. The words in the report must match the model.
Procedural: put the answer back into the story. Does it fit the numbers? Is it a sensible size?

steps: Practice: 48 interns split into 6 equal teams. 6t = 48, so t = 8.
Check: 6 teams of 8 is 48. That matches the story.
8 interns on a team is a sensible size, so the answer is reasonable.
worked.q: Hana solves 3b = 27 and gets b = 81. Is that reasonable?

items.q: The Splash Boat answer is r ≤ 7. Which sentence belongs in the report?

options.fb: That reads it like an equation. r ≤ 7 is a range, so fewer riders are fine too.

options.t: Up to 7 more riders can board: 7, 6, 5 and so on, down to 0.
At least 7 more riders must board.
options.fb: "At least" is ≥. That flips the rule: 8 more riders would make 13 in the boat.

items.q: Gus solved 5n = 65, where n is the balloons in each of 5 equal bunches. He got n = 325. Is that reasonable?

options.fb: That is Gus's mistake. 5n = 65 says 5 TIMES n is 65. Undo × 5 by dividing: 65 ÷ 5.

options.t: No. 5 bunches of 325 is 1,625 balloons, not 65. Divide: n = 13.
Yes, because 325 is a whole number
options.fb: A whole number can still be wrong. Check it: 5 × 325 = 1,625, not 65.

gates.pass: Gus re-solves: 65 ÷ 5 = 13 balloons per bunch. "I knew 325 felt like a lot."

gates.title: Boss Gate · Krank's Desk
gates.prompt: File the last two incidents. Choose the model, solve it, and solve the mascot-head equation.
hints: Conceptual: "at least" is a constraint, so it needs an inequality. "Exactly" is one value, so it needs an equation.
Procedural: write the model with a variable, then undo the operation on both sides.

steps: Practice clue: "The coaster needs at least 20 riders. 6 are on."

items.q: The Ferris wheel needs at least 30 riders for its big night spin. 18 are on. Which model shows how many more riders, x, it needs?

options.fb: = means exactly 12 more. "At least" lets more riders get on too, so it is a range.
≤ means 30 or fewer. "At least 30" means 30 or MORE, which is ≥.
18x means 18 groups of x. The new riders are added to the 18, not multiplied.

items.label: Ferris wheel · x + 18 ≥ 30, so x ≥
items.aria: the fewest more riders the Ferris wheel needs

fb.msg: 48 is 30 + 18. Undo + 18 by subtracting 18 from both sides.

items.fbDefault: Subtract 18 from both sides of x + 18 ≥ 30.

items.label: Mascot heads · 2 heads weigh exactly 9 pounds: 2w = 9, so w =

fb.msg: 18 is 9 × 2. Two heads weigh 9 pounds, so one head weighs LESS than 9. Divide by 2.
7 is 9 − 2. 2w means 2 times w, so divide both sides by 2.

gates.pass: Mr. Krank reads every line. "Equations where it's exact. Inequalities where it's a limit. Print it."

journal.heading: Lesson 8-7 — what the park report taught us
rows: "Exactly 24 in all" is one value: 3c = 24. "No more than 12" is a constraint: r + 5 ≤ 12.
Is, equals, exactly, in all: equation (=). At least (≥), no more than (≤), more than (>), fewer than (<): inequality.
Use inverse operations on both sides. 3c = 24 gives c = 8. m ÷ 4 = 15 gives m = 60. r + 5 ≤ 12 gives r ≤ 7.
Put the answer back in the story. 5 × 325 is 1,625, not 65, so n = 325 is not reasonable. n = 13 is.
journal.quote: "Exactly 24 funnel cakes. Write that down. Equations never lie." — Bandit

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 8-7 (Equations and Inequalities Problem Solving) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. It covers only this lesson: choosing an equation for an exact value or an inequality for a constraint, solving the model with inverse operations, and checking that the answer is reasonable.
standards: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering which values make it true; use substitution to determine whether a given number makes an equation or inequality true
